source.title: Forecasting with Deep Pooled Panel Neural Networks
source.authors: I. Chronopoulos; Katerina Chrysikou; G. Kapetanios; James Mitchell; Aristeidis Raftapostolos

record.file_problem: none; full paper and online appendix are present
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses double descent and reports forecast comparisons with and without lasso penalization, but does not measure test error across model size, epochs, or sample size, or locate an interpolation threshold.
record.gate_note: The paper's own lasso-versus-unpenalized forecast-error comparisons are recorded as results about regularization, not as tests of a double-descent curve: neither table measures a peak or whether it disappears. The discussion of double descent in Remark 2 also cites other work; cited findings are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It never varies model size, epochs, sample size or parameter count against the interpolation point, and never measures a test-error peak. Its only related result is a 7-day-ahead RMSE comparison of unpenalized versus lasso-penalized networks (Tables B.10–B.11), chosen by cross-validation. That result bears on whether explicit regularization helps, not on whether a double-descent curve exists or vanishes under tuned regularization. Remark 2 explains double descent by citing Belkin et al. (2019), Hastie et al. (2022) and Kelly et al. (2022); it does not test it.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but it understates the authors' claim. The authors say they 'find evidence of the double descent phenomenon' (Introduction; Section 4.1.3). They also say penalizing 'unambiguously leads to less accurate forecasts' (footnote 5). Their evidence is only that unpenalized deep models forecast better than lasso-penalized ones, and they explain this by citing Hastie et al. (2022) and Kelly et al. (2022). The 'unambiguously' wording is not borne out for the deep time-series model: 7 of its 14 ratios exceed 1 (r9, r13, r14, r22, r23, r26 and others). No curve is shown.
record.recipe_differences: No direct test of the original double-descent method; the paper reports panel forecasting results and selected comparisons with lasso-penalized models.
record.method_sensitivity: Forecast-error comparisons vary by model type, country, and whether the aggregate or disaggregated stringency index is used.

fits_no_version.finding: At 7 days ahead (Tables B.10–B.11), the unpenalized deep pooled model beats its lasso-penalized counterpart in all 14 country × policy-index cells (ratios 0.54–0.81). For the deep time-series model, 7 of 14 cells exceed 1 (up to 1.081), so the penalty sometimes helps there. No significance tests are reported for these ratios.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In cross-validated deep forecasting networks for COVID-19 panels, dropping an explicit ℓ1 penalty often improves out-of-sample RMSE. The gain is consistent for the pooled model but mixed for the unit-specific model. No capacity curve is measured.

record.problems: The lasso comparison covers only 7-days-ahead COVID-19 forecasts and does not sweep model complexity, epochs, or sample size. It reports no uncertainty estimates for the lasso-comparison ratios.

untested.parts: No sweep of model size and no test error around the interpolation threshold. Width and depth are chosen by cross-validation, and error by size is not reported.
No test-error curve over training epochs. Early stopping is used, and the training curves are not reported.
No comparison of test error across training-sample sizes near an interpolation threshold. The expanding windows are not analysed this way.
No capacity sweep in any model class.
No measure of effective complexity, and no peak locations.

No peak is measured. Label noise and variance are not manipulated. There is no test of multiple descent, and no test of whether tuned regularization removes a peak. The lasso-versus-unpenalized comparison does not measure a capacity curve.
No effective-parameter count, and no re-expression of a capacity curve.

record.verdict_notes: All rows are correctly linked to ['none'] with state cannot_determine: an RMSE ratio between penalized and unpenalized models cannot show a peak or its removal. The authors' framing ('evidence of double descent') goes beyond what the data show and should not be read as a test of V1 or V6. Regularization strength λ was itself cross-validated on a grid, so this is a comparison against a tuned lasso, not a sweep of regularization strength. The text contains no instructions.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or test-error curve around the training-set interpolation threshold.
No test-error curve over training epochs.
No comparison of test error across training-sample sizes near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep across model classes or interpolation points.
No common effective-complexity measure is tested against peak locations.

The study compares forecast accuracy with and without lasso but does not test whether label noise or variance drives a peak, whether multiple peaks arise, or whether regularization removes a double-descent peak.
No effective-parameter count or re-expression of a capacity curve is tested.
